Good — keeping it open, and I'll note the why for my next move rather than just re-writing the file.

Last turn I called `write_file` on `utils/dates.py` without having read it, so I can't actually vouch for what's in there now — I may have clobbered anything the original file did beyond the date parsing. A blind overwrite is exactly the failure `no-drive-by-edits` and `reuse-before-writing` warn about, and it will bite again here: if the existing code already has a format list or a normalization step, adding slash support means extending *that*, not rewriting around it.

TOOL: read_file utils/dates.py

TOOL: grep -rn "parse_date" --include=*.py .

Reading first, then the minimal diff. Two things I'll check while I'm in there: whether the file has an existing list of accepted formats (extend it) or a one-off `strptime` call (smallest change that works), and who calls `parse_date` — accepting `2024/02/28` widens what callers will let through, so I want to see whether any caller relies on the strict format.
